Selected projects

Land Cover Change, Pakuwon City, Surabaya

Individual · Google Earth Engine, ArcMap · 2010–2025

Supervised classification of Landsat imagery (Random Forest, 100 trees; NDVI, NDBI, MNDWI features) for 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2025, with 5-fold cross-validation and change mapping over a ~1,252 ha study area.

85.6–94.7%overall accuracy
0.70–0.88Kappa
+160 habuilt-up, 2010–2025

Built-up land grew from 30.2% to 43.0% of the area; about 80 ha of vegetation converted to built-up land.

Limits I documented: Landsat 5/7 vs 8/9 sensor differences affect 2010 comparisons, and apparent “loss” is likely classification noise, so net change is the figure to trust.

Road Connectivity & Accessibility, Kebayoran Baru, Jakarta

Individual · QGIS, Google Earth Engine, ArcMap

Network analysis of 35 activity centers (hospitals, malls, markets, campuses, MRT stations, terminal) using OpenStreetMap roads, service areas at 500 m / 1 km / 2 km, and WorldPop population in GEE.

1.52Beta index
0.52Gamma index
45.1%population within 500 m

80.9% of residents fall within 1 km of an activity center. Also compared straight-line buffers with network service areas to show how buffers overstate real reach.

Contour & Water Flow Direction, Campus Elevation Points

Group project (7 members) · Python, IDW · My role: field surveyor and analyst

Collected the elevation points in the field with a Hi-Target GNSS RTK system (base and rover with handheld controller), then ran the analysis: cleaned 278 points (removed 9 nodata and 6 outlier values), interpolated with IDW, drew 1 m contours, and estimated overall flow with a fitted plane and 2,000-run bootstrap.

263valid points
~1.1°mean slope
240°flow azimuth (SW)

Reported honestly: R² of 0.32 and no independent check points, so results describe general direction only.

Spatial Interaction Gravity Model, Aceh Province

Individual · Excel, ArcMap · 2024 data

Gravity model of 22 districts/cities against the provincial capital, classified into three hierarchy levels (7 / 7 / 8) and mapped as hierarchy and interaction maps.

0.92Spearman, rank vs distance
0.44Spearman, rank vs population

A sensitivity test on the distance exponent showed only 2 districts changing class, so the weakest-interaction group stayed the same.
